references.text: The account of David coming to the priest Ahimelech at Nob and eating the bread of the Presence when he and his men were hungry. This is the Old Testament event Jesus refers to in his answer to the Pharisees.
Matthew's parallel account where Jesus, in the same way, answers the Pharisees by referring to David who ate the bread of the Presence, which was not lawful for him to eat.
Mark's parallel account where Jesus answers with the reference to David eating the bread of the Presence when he was hungry, he and those who were with him.
Matthew's parallel account about the disciples picking grain on the Sabbath and the Pharisees' accusation, which is the context for Jesus' answer.
Mark's parallel account about the disciples picking grain on the Sabbath and the Pharisees' objection.
The immediate context in Luke: the disciples pick grain on the Sabbath and the Pharisees ask a question, leading to Jesus' answer in verse 3.
